sources.title: Models.dev Muse Glimmer 30B record
sources.evidence: Traces the baseline to Meta's announcement, official Hugging Face repository and developer page; catalog claims were independently checked.

sources.title: Introducing Muse Glimmer: An Open Agentic Model That Runs on Your Device
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Meta's August 10 launch explicitly calls Muse Glimmer a 30-billion-parameter model and releases its weights. Distillation from Muse Spark is a compressed student relationship, not unchanged-model lineage; the teacher's parameter counts do not transfer.

sources.title: Muse Glimmer Model Card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The exact model's official architecture table still reports approximately 29.6B total including vision, with a dense causal Transformer and perception encoder. No separately labeled active or activated parameter count is given. The optional DFlash drafter is a separate release.

sources.title: Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model, v3 (October 23, 2026)
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 and searched the complete October 23 v3 text. Table 1 reports approximately 29.6B total, approximately 25.16B Transformer blocks, separate untied 1.34B input/output embeddings and approximately 1.8B perception encoder. Section 2 describes the vision adapter/projection. No active-parameter specification or exact-model active-count comparison is present; active experts describe discarded MoE architecture experiments, not the released dense model.

sources.title: Muse Glimmer developer documentation
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The Model variants table specifies nominal 30B, dense multimodal architecture and default 128K context with longer contexts supported. It does not define an active-parameter count. The documentation identifies Muse Spark distillation and Apache 2.0 open weights.

sources.title: Muse Glimmer 30B checkpoint configuration
sources.evidence: Pinned checkpoint config specifies MuseGlimmerForConditionalGeneration, bfloat16, untied embeddings, text max_position_embeddings 131072, 52 language layers and 50 vision layers; no quantization configuration.

sources.title: Muse Glimmer 30B BF16 checkpoint index
sources.evidence: Direct HTTPS reopened the pinned JSON index successfully on October 27, 2026. Published metadata still explicitly reports total_parameters 29,776,626,688 and total_size 59,553,253,376 bytes, with 1,436 weight-map entries. This re-audit reads metadata only; no weight shards or tensor headers were requested.

sources.title: Muse Glimmer 30B BF16 shard 1 tensor header
sources.evidence: HTTP range requests retrieved only the header. Its 1,347 BF16 weight/bias tensors contain 24,974,971,392 elements; no quantization scale, packed integer or other buffer tensors were present.

sources.title: Muse Glimmer 30B BF16 shard 2 tensor header
sources.evidence: HTTP range requests retrieved only the header. Its 89 BF16 weight/bias tensors contain 4,801,655,296 elements. Together both shard headers reproduce the index total; all names match the complete weight map.

sources.title: Muse Glimmer 30B license
sources.evidence: The official repository's pinned LICENSE contains Apache License, Version 2.0.

sources.title: Transformers Muse Glimmer model implementation
sources.evidence: Cross-check of saved tensor roles: linear, embedding and norm weights/biases are parameters; vision position embeddings are learned. Parameter-free normalization and computed rotary frequencies add no saved tensors. Used only to validate the checkpoint count, not to infer model identity.

sources.title: Original Muse Glimmer developer-page URL
sources.evidence: The web browsing tool could not access this original URL. Direct HTTPS succeeded and redirected to https://dev.meta.ai/models/muse-glimmer, whose content links the official model card and documentation.

sources.title: Meta is back with Muse Glimmer: local, agentic, multimodal, and open source
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The launch integration team's architecture discussion describes a nominal 30B model as a 28B text decoder plus a 2B vision encoder, and explicitly separates the optional DFlash drafter. These rounded component sizes corroborate scope but are not an active-parameter convention; no active count is stated.

name.note: Exact repository and technical-report name; 30B is the nominal model designation.

developer.note: Meta Superintelligence Labs is the developing organization.

family.note: Normalized Muse series label, consistent with the model's name and its explicitly identified Muse Spark teacher; no teacher specifications are transferred.

release_date.note: Meta's dated announcement explicitly introduces the model and releases its weights that day. Later paper revisions and HF repository creation are not the public launch date.

open_weights.note: Meta announces open weights and publishes the complete BF16 checkpoint.

license.note: The checkpoint's actual license file agrees with Meta's release announcement.

parameters_b.note: Retain 29.776626688B: the pinned official BF16 index explicitly publishes 29,776,626,688 total parameters, independently reopened October 27. This includes vision encoder, adapter and projection and excludes the separately distributed DFlash drafter. Meta's card/paper specify approximately 29.6B and the launch/docs use nominal 30B; those supported nominal figures are not erased by the checkpoint discrepancy. The original audit's header verification and component breakdown are preserved; no weights or tensor census were needed in this pass.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 review of the exact card, full v3 technical report, launch and current documentation found no separately defined active count. Exact-name active/activated searches and later Meta Spark 1.3, Wonder and Spark Open reports/cards found no qualifying Glimmer comparison convention. The paper's active experts concern experimental MoE candidates, not Glimmer. Dense architecture, total size and rounded text/vision component sizes do not establish per-token participation; vision use depends on the input. Teacher and sibling model counts do not transfer.

architecture.note: Dense decoder-only causal Transformer with a separate ViT-G/14 perception encoder and vision adapter/projection; 52 language layers, GQA and repeating three local/one global attention layers. Not MoE.

context_window.note: Exact configured default is 131,072 tokens. Card says 131,072+ and docs permit longer contexts without an exact supported upper bound; retain configured default.

modalities.note: The model card and technical-report table explicitly list text/image inputs and text output. The report additionally allows video as a sequence of frames and the implementation exposes that path, but Meta states it is not explicitly optimized for video; retain the declared modality list.

reasoning.note: Model card documents low, medium, high and xhigh reasoning strengths.

tool_call.note: Primary sources explicitly document function/tool calling and the report's request format includes agent tool invocations.

description.value: Muse Glimmer 30B is a dense multimodal model from Meta Superintelligence Labs, distilled from Muse Spark for local agents, tool use, coding, and image understanding, with weights released under Apache 2.0.
description.note: Retains directly supported purpose, teacher and modalities while adding confirmed dense architecture and avoiding presenting nominal 30B as an exact count.

patch.description: Muse Glimmer 30B is a dense multimodal model from Meta Superintelligence Labs, distilled from Muse Spark for local agents, tool use, coding, and image understanding, with weights released under Apache 2.0.
patch.notes: The published BF16 checkpoint index reports 29.776626688B parameters, including the perception encoder and vision adapter/projection; the separate DFlash drafter is excluded. Meta's card and report give approximately 29.6B, while 30B is the nominal model designation. Active parameters are not separately specified; dense architecture does not establish an all-components per-token count. The configured default context is 131,072 tokens; Meta also advertises longer contexts without an exact upper limit. Meta lists text/image inputs; the report also describes video ingestion as a sequence of frames, without explicit video optimization.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit: retained 29.776626688B total from freshly reopened official pinned index metadata, with Meta's approximate 29.6B and nominal 30B specifications distinguished. Reopened the launch, exact card, full October 23 report, current developer docs and Hugging Face's integration article; checked later Meta source caches and fresh exact-name active/activated searches. No qualifying active-count disclosure or research-team comparison convention was found, so active remains explicitly null/undisclosed. No weight shards or tensor census were requested. Preserved all 12 unrelated field assessments and the previously accepted component breakdown.
